direction_as_read: positive for functional dyspepsia symptoms in two trials, one of them placebo controlled; null on blood pressure in one trial; unresolved in inflammatory bowel disease
summary: Three labels print Mastic Gum 1000 mg, two with a digestive positioning. In functional dyspepsia, a placebo RCT at 350 mg three times daily (19961914, 148 patients) improved symptoms but names no primary outcome, and a crossover at 1.4 g/day (41197785) was positive on named primary outcomes against no intervention, without placebo. In well-controlled hypertension, 42885189 found no blood pressure difference at 1500 or 2800 mg/day. In inflammatory bowel disease, 30450689 reports within-group and marker changes at 2.8 g/day and no primary between-group result in the abstract.
question_for_clinician: Recommend no credit from this review. 41197785 meets rule 2 for a capsule of mastic alone on a named primary outcome, without placebo and at 1.4 g/day; 19961914 is placebo controlled at about the label's amount but names no primary outcome. Do these two support a digestive purpose at the printed 1000 mg, or does the lack of a placebo trial with a named primary outcome keep it at no credit?
